short_description: Request for Advice: Information Management Considerations Following SFT Decommissioning
description:
Good morning,

Further to the attached, we are seeking your advice on information management, privacy, and records management considerations associated with the decommissioning of the Secure File Transfer (SFT) system on 30 November 2026.

The Commonwealth Prac Payment (CPP) team currently uses SFT to receive information from higher education providers for Exceptional Circumstances assessments and routine program reporting. These processes involve the exchange of student personal and, at times, sensitive information.

As part of transition planning, we were in touch with the legal team to seek advice on Privacy. They recommended we reach out to your area.   We also contacted the Managed File Transfer (MFT) team to discuss the proposed solution who advised that MFT doesn’t suit the CPP BAU business need, and that email may be a suitable alternative for information exchange. We are seeking your advice on whether this approach is appropriate from an information management perspective and, if so, what controls should be implemented.
Specifically, we would appreciate guidance on:

  *   Whether the proposed email-based approach aligns with departmental privacy, information management, and records management requirements.
  *   Whether the use of appropriate email classifications and handling instructions would provide sufficient protection for personal and sensitive information.
  *   Any additional controls, safeguards, or governance measures that should be considered before implementation.

Information received via email would continue to be stored and managed in accordance with existing record-keeping requirements within a restricted-access SharePoint environment.

Subject to your advice, the CPP team will update relevant procedures and communicate any approved process changes to participating providers.

We would appreciate any recommendations regarding the suitability of this approach and any information management requirements that should be addressed prior to implementation.

Kind regards,

LC

short_description: System Issue: Employment Outcome Tracking Not Aligning with TtW Policy for Pre-existing Employment and PCW Participants
description:
Hi Digital Solutions Support Team

I would like to raise a system issue that has been identified through a recent policy review of a Transition to Work (TtW) participant record. Our investigation has identified that the Workforce Australia Online for Providers (WFAOP) system is currently allowing Employment Outcomes to track and become claimable in circumstances that are not consistent with TtW policy requirements.

Issue Summary

The issue relates to participants who:
Have an assessed Partial Capacity to Work (PCW).
Are in Pre-existing Employment and receiving an Income Support Payment at the commencement of the Outcome period.

Under current TtW policy, where an Employment Outcome is based on a Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment, participants who are receiving an Income Support Payment must increase their earnings sufficiently to reduce their Income Support Payment to nil before an Employment Outcome can be achieved.

However, we have identified scenarios where the system is instead tracking Outcomes based on declared hours (JEHR average hours) rather than assessing the required income reduction to nil criteria. This appears to occur where the participant has a Part-Time Activity Test and/or a Partial Capacity to Work assessment. We assume the system is basing its assessment on a measurement against achieving the PCW hours such as 15 - 22 hours.

JSID 29033170, 12 Week Employment Outcome became available (effective date 28/07/2026) despite the participant not meeting the policy requirements for a Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment. Instead, the system tracked the Outcome using an average hours methodology based on the participant's PCW and activity test settings.

Business Impact
This issue is creating situations where:

Employment Outcomes may be incorrectly generated and claimed and Providers receive Outcome Payments to which they are not entitled.
Recovery activity may subsequently be required.

Requested Investigation

Could the IT team please investigate:

Whether Outcome tracking logic for a Partial Capacity to Work participants receiving Income Support Payments is correctly applying the Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment requirements within WFAOP.

Please let me know if further information or examples are required.

Kind regards,


Sheree O'Dea
Program  Manager

Transition to Work | Employment Services Programs Branch
Delivery and Partnerships Division
Australian Government Department of Employment and Workplace Relations

short_description: Request for Dynatrace Analysis – Intermittent TM1 Web Performance and Login Issues
description:
Hi Enterprise Management,

We are currently investigating an intermittent issue affecting our IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) environment and are seeking assistance from the Enterprise Management team to determine whether Dynatrace has captured any information that may help identify the root cause.

Servers
---------
EPREWEB200 - TM1 Web Server
EPREAPP212	- Planning Analytics Server

Issue Summary
-----------------
Approximately one week ago, users began reporting periods where TM1 Web becomes sluggish or, in some cases, the TM1 Web login page fails to appear altogether.

The issue appears to occur intermittently and has generally been observed during the following periods:

Approximately 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM
Approximately 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM

Outside of these periods, the environment typically performs normally.

During some occurrences, the IBM Semeru Runtime Binary (javaw.exe) process on the TM1 Web server has been observed consuming in excess of 90% CPU utilisation, peaking at approximately 99%.

However, during a separate occurrence yesterday afternoon where the TM1 Web login page failed to load, CPU utilisation appeared normal. This suggests the underlying cause may not be solely related to CPU consumption.

We have also received a report from a user who experienced the login page issue at approximately 8:00 PM last night, at a time when they were the only user accessing the system.

Findings to Date
-------------------
Our investigation has identified:

- Intermittent TM1 Web performance degradation.
- Occasional failure of the TM1 Web login page to load.
- Browser console errors indicating: "No data received from server", JavaScript errors within TM1 Web application components.
- A TM1 Web javacore generated during one of the incidents containing: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
- Significant garbage collection activity.
- Evidence of TM1 Web request processing activity at the time of the failure.

Could the Enterprise Management team review the available Dynatrace data covering the period from approximately one week ago to advise whether any anomalies have been identified that might provide additional insight into the issue?

Let me know if specific timestamps or supporting logs are required.

Cheers,
Elvis

short_description: Azure SQL pool members are unable to Scope the ADMS production database.
description:
Hi,


The ADMS system has a dependency on these SQL build agent pools -

Settings * Agent pools (ADMS) - Settings<https://dev.azure.com/DigitalSolutionsDivision/ADMS/_settings/agentqueues?queueId=190&view=jobs>



[cid:image001.png@01DD570B.FC219920]


Over the last month during formal releases we've encountered many of these pool members failing to deploy database artefacts to the live ADMS Production DB.


This is an example of what we encounter during last nights ADMS release -

Pipelines - Run 20261006.1 logs<https://dev.azure.com/DigitalSolutionsDivision/ADMS/_build/results?buildId=1104160&view=logs&j=0ff409b1-0d17-50a2-fc4e-01f72eec43ff&t=423b483e-4f05-5139-03b6-c62b8492cc03&s=c2f23cc9-b49b-5971-bdfa-5e6430153f6c>


Error -
##[error]Error executing ADMSApprenticeship.dacpac, please ask a DBA *** Could not deploy package.Unable to connect to target server ''DBP_SKS_APPS01.application.enet,14331''. Please verify the connection information such as the server name, login credentials, and firewall rules for the target server.A network-related or instance-specific error occurred while establishing a connection to SQL Server. The server was not found or was not accessible. Verify that the instance name is correct and that SQL Server is configured to allow remote connections. (provider: TCP Provider, error: 0 - The wait operation timed out.)The wait operation timed out


This implies the SQL agent within the pool cannot scope our ADMS production database.  The workaround has been to keep retrying the failing pipeline, until we get allocated a healthy SQL agent.


These agent instances are known as being problematic - ECOEADO001_SQL_DO001_PRD01 and ECOEADO002_SQL_DO002_PRD01.  (There may be many more).


We need every SQL agent within this pool to be reviewed as to whether it can scope the ADMS DB and appropriate action taken.


Happy to assist.


Regards,

Jason

short_description: Openshift intermittent LDAP authentication issues - Unknown certificate authority
description:
Please assign to TSD Cyber Security team

All 3 of our Openshift clusters have been experiencing intermittent LDAP authentication issues for several weeks (around the time that the production CA certificate was renewed). We have an automation job that connects to ldaps://nation.radix:636 which pulls user/group information out of AD in order to grant access to Openshift.

error: could not connect to the LDAP server: LDAP Result Code 200 "Network Error": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

The job now intermittently fails around 50% of the time and will cause users to not be able to log in.

I have checked that all previous and current nation.radix CAs are in our trusted CA bundle. The fact that it is intermittent makes me lean towards the nation domain controllers, rather than an Openshift configuration issue.

I have also tested the service account 'service_ocp_bind' which is used to connect to AD for the automated job.
LDAP searches work fine when targetting ldap://nation.radix:389 (insecure), though fail when targeting ldaps://nation.radix:636 (secure)

ldapsearch -LLL -v -x -H ldaps://nation.radix:636 -D 'NATION\Service_ocp_bind' -W -b 'OU=Restricted,OU=Users,OU=Department,DC=nation,DC=radix' dn                                                        
                                                                                                                                             
ldap_sasl_bind(SIMPLE): Can't contact LDAP server (-1)


I have also tested against singular DCs (rather than nation.radix) and this produces the same error as above

Subject: LEX 2614 - Internal Review Request - MITAS, Peter - Response due 14 October 2026 [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Dear Nicky and Zane,

Mr Peter Mitas (the Applicant) has made an internal review request under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (FOI Act).  The Applicant is seeking review of a decision made by the department on 4 September 2026 refusing access to documents sought under the following request;

1.             The access or audit log for my participant record on the platform, showing which users and organisations have viewed, accessed, opened, exported, downloaded or printed my information and on what dates, from 1 June 2026 to the date of processing.
2.             Documents describing the categories of participant information visible to Inclusive Employment Australia provider staff on the platform, including user-role definitions, permission matrices or access-level documentation, current as at June to July 2026.
3.             Documents describing whether and how provider staff can search, export, download or print participant records, including assessment documents.
4.             Documents describing the operation and scope of the "sensitive record" mechanism as it operates within the platform, including which data fields it suppresses from provider view and any document considering whether its scope can be extended.
5.             Documents describing which Department is the data custodian of the platform, and which Department controls provider staff access permissions within it.
6.             Documents recording what participant information was transmitted to, or made accessible by, an Inclusive Employment Australia provider in connection with my Customer Reference Number on or about 9 June 2026, and the basis on which that transmission or access occurred.

A copy of the Applicant’s internal review request is attached, along with his subsequent comments and corrections for your review. While the request is quite lengthy, the Applicant’s primary contention is the adequacy of searches. As such, we request your business area to undertake fresh searches and respond to the Information Law Team (ILT) by COB 14 October 2026.

Action required by you


  1.  Search and retrieve all documents within the possession of the department at the time the request was received that are within the scope of the FOI request. This also includes identifying and consulting with other line areas who may have documents within their possession relevant to the scope of the FOI request.
  2.  Collate any sensitivities associated with releasing documents to the applicant and/or publishing documents to the department’s disclosure log. Your description of the specific harm or damage that would or could reasonably result from disclosure of the documents will assist us in considering whether any FOI Act exemptions<https://www.oaic.gov.au/freedom-of-information/freedom-of-information-guidance-for-government-agencies/guidance-on-handling-a-freedom-of-information-request/legal-definitions-and-questions/exemptions-and-conditional-exemptions-under-the-freedom-of-information-act-1982> might apply.
  3.  Should no documents exist, please provide a comprehensive list of searches undertaken, and reasons why documents cannot be located.  This information will be relayed to the Applicant to help them understand why documents are not being provided to them.
  4.  by 14 October 2026 – provide us with a SES-signed Document Search Minute (DSM) for each line area in possession of documents within the scope of the FOI request (including your overarching DSM as the lead line area). Documents (and attachments) must be provided to us in a PDF format.

*There is a current issue with converting emails to PDF. Please open emails in Outlook and select Archive Mail. Using open with > Kofax in File Explorer changes aspects of the PDF. A useful Kofax guide to archiving emails in general can be found here: Kofax PDF - Troubleshooting Metadata Issues<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0017428>

Please have group policy change the port into one of the available 5-digit range ports

(SCP) is a unified endpoint software service that authenticates and redirects HTTP/S and non-HTTP web traffic from corporate devices to Skyhigh Security Service Edge (SSE) solutions like Secure Web Gateway, Cloud Firewall, and Private Access. [1, 2, 3]

short_description: Request for Investigation – DMARC Validation Failure for ServiceNow Notifications
description:
OFFICIAL

Hi DEWR Team,

We are seeking your assistance with an email delivery issue affecting ServiceNow notifications sent via the employment.gov.au email relay.

Our Microsoft team has identified that notifications originating from Optus ServiceNow are failing DMARC validation because the identity aligned by DMARC is the original sender's domain (optus.com.au), while the DKIM signature applied by the relay is for employment.gov.au. As a result, DMARC validation fails and the emails are not being delivered as expected.

Based on the investigation, it has been suggested that ARC (Authenticated Received Chain) support on the employment.gov.au relay may help preserve the original authentication results and allow downstream systems to validate the messages correctly.

Could you please investigate whether ARC is supported, or can be enabled, on the employment.gov.au mail relay? Additionally, if there are any alternative solutions or recommendations to address this issue, we would appreciate your guidance. Please let us know if you require any additional information, logs, or sample messages to assist with the investigation.

Regards,

Syed Waris

short_description: Remove Legacy Report Message Outlook Add-in
description:
Good afternoon Workplace Systems team,

The Cyber Governance and Education Team is seeking assistance to remove the legacy Report Message Outlook add-in.

A recent Microsoft update introduced built-in email reporting functionality within Outlook. As a result, users now have two separate options available to report suspicious emails. As the Microsoft-provided functionality now serves the same purpose, the legacy Report Message add-in is no longer required.

Removing the legacy add-in will reduce user confusion and provide staff with a single, consistent method for reporting suspicious emails.

There is a degree of urgency to this request as phishing awareness activities are currently underway as part of Cyber Awareness Month. Having two reporting buttons available during these activities may create unnecessary confusion for users when determining how to report suspicious emails.

We appreciate that this request comes at short notice. If possible, we would be grateful if this work could be prioritised.

This request has the approval of Cecilia Lau, Acting IT Security Advisor (ITSA).

If there are any other dependencies, approvals needed to progress this request, please let us know.

Microsoft recommends transitioning from the Report Message and Report Phishing add-ins to the built-in Outlook Report button and provides guidance on removing the legacy add-ins. Further information is available here:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/submissions-users-report-message-add-in-configure

Your help is much appreciated.

Kind Regards,
Dan

I checked the folder in Classic Outlook for Windows and its the same issue.

Filter = Off
Group By = None
Reviewed Advanced View Settings and found no filters applied.
Confirmed Outlook is connected to Exchange.
Opened the folder properties for TEMP NR.

There is an indexing or synchronisation issue affecting the shared mailbox folder.
A retention policy, mailbox rule, or automated process has affected the folder contents.
The folder contents have become corrupted or are not displaying correctly despite the emails being searchable.

The key point is that Outlook Search finds the emails and identifies TEMP NR as their location, but the folder itself appears empty.

Thanks.

short_description: Secure SharePoint setup for CTS Rounds 4 and 5
description:
Good morning,

I hope this email finds you well.

Thank you for all your assistance in setting up the previous secure SharePoint sites for the Commonwealth Teaching Scholarships (CTS) Program. These sites have been invaluable in meeting the program's additional security requirements due to the sensitive nature of the materials stored.

The CTS Program is due to move into its fourth round in November 2026. We continue to receive an average of 3,500 applications per round, with 1,000 applicants awarded a scholarship. This results in a large volume of files that must be stored in accordance with the Department's Information Management policy.

With only two rounds remaining, we are requesting that the final two secure SharePoint sites be developed. Establishing both sites will help streamline setup in the lead-up to the final rounds.

I have detailed our requested specifications for both sites below:

Request:
Two standalone SharePoint Online sites where SENSITIVE documents can be stored and only limited users have access to.
The sites used for this program should be kept running till at least 2030 (potentially 2042).

Site name: CTS Round 4
Site owners: Catherine Hobbs, Christine Crowther, Lisa Cox
Document types: PDF, Excel, Word
Size storage: Large (200GB)
Sensitive meaning: Documents will contain personal data including name, DOB, address, email, bank details, and identity documents. All these documents will have 'Sensitive' marking.
Access permissions: Edit access will only be provided to the CTS Team (in Education) and a small number of Education SES staff (around 10-12 in total)

short_description: DEWR Intranet - Update HUB Links on the DEWR Intranet
description:
Hi Luke,

I had a look at whether there was a way to identify references to the old HUB URL without relying solely on a broken link scan through SWOOP.
I've put together a script that scans the PROD intranet SharePoint sites and have attached the resulting report for reference.

The scan checked content within SharePoint Site Pages and categorises matches as:

  *   OLD_URL - references to the old HUB URL (https://hub.goverp.gov.au/sites)
  *   NEW_URL - references to the current HUB URL (https://hub.goverp.gov.au/site)
  *   ROOT_URL_ONLY - references to the HUB root URL (https://hub.goverp.gov.au)

Each row includes the site, page title and the URL category identified. The report does not identify the link text as that would be harder to script, so you'll have to look through all the looks to find the Hub URL. I've filtered the attached report to show PROD sites only.

The main focus would be the OLD_URL entries, as these are candidates for review and update. One advantage of this approach is that it can identify references even where the old URL is still redirecting successfully and therefore may not be detected as a broken link.

At this stage I've only validated the Site Pages content scan. The script also includes functionality to scan navigation links, however I haven't tested that portion yet, so the attached report is based on Site Pages content only.
The scan shouldn't be considered a complete inventory of every possible reference, but it should provide a useful starting point for remediation.

I'll also raise an incident to capture the script, report and approach for future reference if needed.

Regards,
Ignatius

Ignatius Kok
Assistant Director SharePoint Solutions

Subject: RE: Consideration of Weekly Reboot for Workforce Australia Online for Providers Web Servers [SEC=OFFICIAL]




Hello everyone
Garry Francis from our Section's Performance Team has reviewed the server strings that are the heart of the problem (see below) and has suggested some improvements that I also would recommend that ETD consider when they are looking at remediating this issue.

[cid:image001.png@01DD4CF8.C30E0820]

This issue affects not only the 300 SD server string but also the 600SD server string.

I agree that a reboot each week has become a necessity for those server strings and I have discussed this with Ravi Krishnamurthy and there the recommendation is that the reboot occur on Sundays at 8:00AM.

In Summary my teams's advice to ETD is as follows:


  *   That the servers on the IPREAPP300SD and 600SD strings each get a memory upgrade of at least 32 Gb, preferably 64Gb; and
  *   The servers are rebooted each Sunday at 8:00 AM as this has the least impact on the WorkforceAustralia operations

Thanks
James

Analysis:

The reported issue is that the Self-hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) is intermittently becoming disconnected/offline, which causes activities using the SHIR to fail.

The SHIR requires communication with the Azure service endpoints and periodically sends heartbeat information to the backend. Typically, around 20 heartbeats are expected within a 10-minute period. When the heartbeat count drops significantly or heartbeat information is not reported for an extended period, this indicates an interruption in communication and can result in the SHIR being reported as offline.

The key point for further investigation is to determine why the SHIR machine is intermittently losing communication with the required Azure service endpoints and at which layer the communication is being interrupted.

The required network communication and endpoint requirements are documented here: Self-hosted Integration Runtime – Ports and Firewalls<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/create-self-hosted-integration-runtime?tabs=data-factory&utm_source=chatgpt.com#ports-and-firewalls> / Get URL of Azure Relay via UI<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/create-self-hosted-integration-runtime?tabs=data-factory#get-url-of-azure-relay-via-ui>

Could you please engage your internal network/infrastructure team to investigate the intermittent connectivity from the SHIR machine?

To help identify where the communication is being interrupted, we recommend the following:


  *   Check connectivity from EPPCADO001 to all required Azure service endpoints.
  *   Capture network traces directly on the SHIR machine while the issue is occurring.
  *   At the same time, capture traces across the relevant network layers, including the proxy, firewall/security devices, network infrastructure, and other applicable layers.
  *   Correlate the traces using the same timestamps so the network team can determine where the connection is being interrupted.
  *   Check whether any firewall, proxy, security appliance, routing, or other network component is intermittently dropping or interrupting the communication.
  *   Verify that the required endpoints and ports are permitted as documented in the Microsoft documentation.

The Azure Relay endpoint information can be obtained using the following documentation: Get Azure Relay URL for Self-hosted Integration Runtime<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/create-self-hosted-integration-runtime?tabs=data-factory&utm_source=chatgpt.com#get-url-of-azure-relay-via-ui>
A simultaneous network trace from the SHIR machine and the relevant network layers during an actual disconnection will be important to correlate the event and determine where the communication is being interrupted.

As the Self-hosted IR is running on an on-premises Windows server, Microsoft does not have visibility into the customer's internal network path, including the local network, proxy, firewall, security appliances, routing, and other infrastructure components.

These components are managed within the customer's environment. Therefore, we kindly request that the internal network/infrastructure team investigate the connectivity from the SHIR machine and identify the point at which the communication is being interrupted.

Good afternoon ELG,

Please find attached the draft Departmental Assurance Framework for your review and feedback by 12 pm, Friday 2 October 2026.

As discussed at the 10 September meeting, the Framework has been developed by Internal Audit to provide a consistent foundation for how assurance activities are understood, coordinated and leveraged across the department. It aims to improve visibility of assurance activities, support risk-informed decision-making, and strengthen the department's ability to identify assurance gaps, duplication and emerging risks. The Framework is not intended to be a detailed procedural or "how-to" guide. Rather, it outlines the department's assurance principles, roles and responsibilities, governance arrangements, and expectations for assurance planning, coordination and reporting. When reviewing the draft Framework, please consider the following questions:


  *   Does the Framework clearly articulate the department's approach to assurance and how assurance activities contribute to risk-informed decision-making?

short_description: Notification – Scheduled Orphan SQL User Cleanup for Development SQL Servers managed by DBAs
description:
An automated process has been implemented to identify and remove orphaned database users from Development SQL Server environments.

The process will be executed via the Azure DevOps pipeline Remove_OrphanSqlUsers and is scheduled to run daily at 08:00 AM against Development SQL Server instances managed by the DBA Team.

Pipeline https://dev.azure.com/TechnologyandServicesDivision/DBA-Support-Service/_build?definitionId=276&_a=summary

Purpose

The automated process will:

Scan Development SQL Server instances for orphaned database users.
Identify affected SQL instances, databases, user accounts, role memberships, and owned schemas.
Generate audit reports for detected orphan users.
Automatically remove orphaned database users where removal criteria are met.
Record cleanup actions and any exceptions encountered during processing.

Scope

Development SQL Server environments only.
SQL Server instances managed by the DBA Team.

Expected Impact

No outage or service interruption is expected.
The process targets database users only and does not remove SQL Server logins.
Users that cannot be removed automatically due to schema ownership, object ownership, permissions, or other dependencies will be reported for manual review.

Benefits

Improves database security and housekeeping by removing obsolete orphaned users.
Provides consistent auditing and reporting of orphan user remediation activities.
Reduces manual effort associated with orphan user identification and cleanup.

Schedule

Daily execution at 08:00 AM via Azure DevOps Pipeline Remove_OrphanSqlUsers.

Action Required

No action is required unless issues are identified following execution. Any exceptions reported by the process will be reviewed and actioned as required.

short_description: Transition from SFTP to MFT - ongoing business transfer arrangements for shared workspaces
description:
Hi DEWR Service Desk and MFT Team,

We first became aware of the transition from FTP to MFT when our FOI team received the recent communication from DEWR.

Background
Our Information Access team manages the release of information in response to FOI, privacy and other information access requests. As part of this function, the team uses a shared SFTP workspace to manage consultation packages provided to third parties during the FOI process, as well as decision packages provided to applicants. Consultation is undertaken for the majority of FOI matters and often involves multiple third parties. In the last reporting year, the team issued 136 FOI decisions and estimates that more than 300 folders were created within its workspace to support consultations and information releases.

The shared workspace model allows team members to manage transfers efficiently while maintaining internal quality assurance processes. To our knowledge, the team has not experienced any privacy breaches or instances of information being shared with an unintended recipient under the current arrangement. Given the volume of work managed by a small team operating within statutory timeframes, there is concern that moving to a request-by-request transfer model could introduce a significant administrative burden and increase the risk of delays in meeting legislative obligations. We are also aware of several other FWO teams that use shared SFTP workspaces in a similar way to efficiently manage ongoing external information transfers.

Further information requested
We have been unable to identify from the available resources whether MFT supports an equivalent arrangement to the current SFTP shared workspaces used by some FWO teams.

If an equivalent or alternative team-based solution exists, we would appreciate advice on:

  *   Whether each business area is required to submit its own request to establish an arrangement.
  *   What information, approvals or business justification should be included to support such a request.
  *   Any differences in administration, processing, approvals or user management compared with the current SFTP shared workspace model, so that teams can assess impacts and update their procedures accordingly.
  *   Any recommended lead time for business areas to submit requests and establish arrangements ahead of the FTP decommissioning date.


We are currently gathering information to help affected teams plan for the transition and would appreciate any guidance or documentation you can provide.


Regards,

description:

[cid:image003.png@01DD4A77.104390D0]

From: EDUC - People <People@education.gov.au>
Sent: Monday, 21 September 2026 10:49 AM
To: TOLANO,Katherine <Katherine.Tolano@atec.gov.au>
Subject: RE: Request for assistance | How to have my email changed to my preferred name [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Kathy,

Below details are for the link provided for you to follow. Where it states to send information to payroll, you can update your name change via the SDO Portal > Change my personal details tile. Change my personal details - Employee Centre<https://sdoservicemanagement.servicenowcloud.com.au/esc?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=0410a2bf78ac1a10d178040d846d3f97>, noting this link will not work until you have HUB access.

Once you have actioned the below steps, if you wish to make changes to your email, please contact the DEWR IT team servicedesk@dewr.gov.au<mailto:servicedesk@dewr.gov.au> and provide them with the screenshot of change for their reference when you request the change.
Step 1. Update HUB/SAP

Send an email to your Pay Team and advise them you've changed your name.

This is the most important step, as your pay, taxation and superannuation records are tied to your name. It's crucial that these records are accurate.

Your email should mention:

  *   brief explanation as to why you're changing your name
  *   your previous name
  *   your current legal name
  *   your current preferred name.

If you're a CONTRACTOR and your pay isn't handled through HUB, email your Director and ask they reply and confirm it's OK for your name to be changed in the system.

Once your Director has approved, Forward they email to either ICTContractorManagement@dewr.gov.au<mailto:ICTContractorManagement@dewr.gov.au> or procurementandgrants@dewr.gov.au<mailto:procurementandgrants@dewr.gov.au>  depending on the type of your employment.

You also need to notify your employment provider if you've changed your legal name.

You may be asked for evidence.

If you're changing your legal name, you'll almost certainly be asked for documentary evidence. They'll let you know what they require.

Are you only changing your preferred name?

If you're simply changing your preferred name, but you're leaving your legal name unchanged, make this clear in your email. Documentation probably won't be needed in these cases.

SAP/HUB needs to know both your legal name and your preferred name. These are often slightly different. You may prefer to use an informal version of your legal name. You may prefer to use your middle name. Ensure you are clear in your request.

Back to top<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal#top>

Step 2. Contact the Service Desk

Forward the confirmation email from Pay Team (once they've updated SAP/HUB) to Service Desk.

Or, if you're a Contractor, once either of the teams in the prior step have emailed you to confirm the change has been made in their system, forward the email confirmation to servicedesk@dewr.gov.au<mailto:servicedesk@dewr.gov.au> for those changes to be processed for your nation account.

The Service Desk can then make the following changes:

  *   Update your first name in Active Directory.
  *   Add a new email address that corresponds to your new first name in Exchange.
     *   The new address will be set as your main address.
     *   When you send an email to an external person, the main address is the From address.
     *   The old address won't be removed. This allows emails sent to your previous address to arrive in your inbox.
  *   Update the display name on your desk phone.
  *   You may then complete the Create Building Access Card<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=sc_cat_item&table=sc_cat_item&sys_id=2d0df01787c34150f184edf83cbb357c> form with the updated information.

Back to top<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal#top>

Step 3. Notify other business areas (where appropriate)

Not all applications or business areas will notice that your name has changed. You are required to notify the appropriate teams separately.

Travel and Credit Cards

Staff with an official credit card must notify their department or agency's Travel and Credit Cards team when their name changes.

Security Clearances

The Australian Government Security Vetting Agency (AGSVA) and your agency Protective Security Team will need to be notified of your name change.

  *   Clearances granted post December 2012: You will need to submit a Change of Circumstance Notification form via AGSVA electronic epack system using the same user name and password that you had when you completed your security clearance.
Once you have submitted the change of circumstance notification form, you will received an automatic email from AGSVA.
This email is then forward to AGSVA <agsva.vsc@defence.gov.au><mailto:agsva.vsc@defence.gov.au> and attached a certified copy for the reason of the name change (Marriage, Divorce, Change of Name certificate etc.) and cc your agency Protective Security Team.
  *   Clearances that were granted pre December 2012: will need to complete a paper version of the change of circumstance notification form<https://www.defence.gov.au/AGSVA/maintaining-your-clearance.asp> and email it to AGSVA <agsva.vsc@defence.gov.au><mailto:agsva.vsc@defence.gov.au>  along with a certified copy for the reason of the name change (Marriage, Divorce, Change of Name certificate etc.) and cc your agency Protective Security Team.
Kind Regards,

Emma Proctor
A/g Assistant Director
HR Operations | People | People, Parliamentary and Communications
Australian Government Department of Education

description:
The TGA inbound integration has stopped processing because the Azure Function App cannot establish an outbound HTTPS connection to ws.training.gov.au.

The application code is functioning correctly. The failure occurs before any data is retrieved, while attempting to download the TGA WSDL from the endpoint.

Observed Behaviour

Item	DetailsDestination Host	ws.training.gov.au
Resolved IP	165.12.212.75
Port	TCP 443
Source Subnet	10.83.194.160/27
DNS Resolution	Successful
Connection Status	Connection timeout after approximately 21 seconds
Error	SocketException 10060

Kudu Connectivity Test Results

Test	ResultHost Resolution	Successful
IPv4 Address	165.12.212.75
TCP Connection	Timed out after approximately 21 seconds
Outcome	Unable to connect to server

Business Impact

Item	DetailsLast Successful Coverage	Around 17 September
Missed Runs	18, 19, 20 and 21 September
Data Impact	No data corruption or partial processing
Current State	No data written to SQL or ARMS because processing stops before download
Risk	TGA catalogue data becoming stale
Future Risk	If unresolved beyond approximately 24 September, the inbound lookback window may need to be manually extended to prevent missing older changes

Additional Investigation

We compared connectivity from different locations:

Test Location	ResultOffice Workstation (via corporate proxy)	Successfully reached ws.training.gov.au at approximately 01:04 today
Azure Function App	Timed out connecting to 165.12.212.75:443

This indicates the TGA endpoint is reachable externally and the issue appears to be specific to the Azure outbound network path for subnet 10.83.194.160/27.

Assessment

The issue is likely related to:

Azure Firewall rule
Network routing
NSG configuration
Outbound egress path
Firewall/Application Rule using an outdated destination IP

No application code changes can resolve this issue because the failure occurs before application-level communication begins.

Requested Action

Please assign this incident to the Network Team for investigation of the Azure outbound connectivity path from subnet 10.83.194.160/27 to ws.training.gov.au (165.12.212.75) on TCP 443.

Please verify:

Firewall and outbound access rules.
Routing configuration for the subnet.
NSG restrictions.
Azure Firewall/Application Rules.
Whether access is configured using hostname or a fixed IP address.
Any recent network or firewall changes that may have impacted connectivity.

Logs and additional test results can be provided if required.

Request for information about open period records under section 31(2) of the Archives Act 1983

Response required by: 3/11/2026

National Archives of Australia has received an inquiry regarding open period records created by the CA 8245 - Department of Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs, National Office.

We have not been able to locate these records in our custody and believe they may be held by your agency.

Under section 31 of the Archives Act 1983, National Archives is required to provide access to open period records that are in the custody of a Commonwealth institution and are not exempt from access. Agencies are required to assist National Archives to meet these obligations.

We request your agency to search for information about relevant records. Please see the attached checklist for details of the inquiry, searches completed by National Archives and contextual information.

To allow us to meet our service standards, please respond within 30 business days.

For the context of this specific request, please check the contents of the identified record and advise if the requested information is located within the specific index cards.

If confirmed please provide/confirm the below details.

We will then assist the client to submit formal applications for access under the Archives Act.

If records are not able to be identified or have been destroyed

short_description: Teams Meeting - Recording and Transcript Access
description:
Issue Summary
Our team uses Microsoft Teams Group/Channel calendars to schedule stakeholder meetings for project delivery activities. Currently, only the person who creates the meeting can access the meeting recording and transcript afterwards.

Expected Result
Project team members who attended the meeting, or who have access to the relevant Team/Channel, can access the recording and transcript to support meeting minutes, action tracking and project record management.

Actual Result
Only the meeting organiser can access the recording and transcript, requiring manual sharing and creating delays in completing post-meeting activities.

Business Impact
This creates unnecessary administrative effort and delays in:
- Preparing meeting minutes.
- Managing action items and follow-up activities.
- Saving project artefacts and records.
- Supporting continuity when the meeting organiser is unavailable.

Request
Please confirm whether this behaviour is expected and whether there is a configuration or alternative approach that would allow recordings and transcripts from Teams Group/Channel meetings to be accessible to authorised team members.

short_description: 20260921 *INITIAL CONTACT MADE* Poly Headset Dongle Not Detected by Windows or Teams
description:
Hi Service Desk,

My Poly headset dongle appears to have stopped working.

The headset functions correctly when connected directly to my DEWR laptop using the USB cable. However, when I disconnect the cable and connect the Poly USB dongle, the headset is not detected in either Microsoft Teams or Windows.

I have performed the following checks:

Connected the Poly headset via USB cable to the same laptop port and confirmed it works correctly.
Connected the Poly USB dongle to the same port and confirmed the headset is not detected.
Checked Microsoft Teams device settings and the Poly headset does not appear as an available audio device when using the dongle.
Checked Windows Sound settings and the Poly device is not listed when using the dongle.
Checked Device Manager and the Poly dongle does not appear.
Tested the dongle in multiple USB ports with the same result.
When the dongle is connected, I hear the headset announcements: "Power on", "Battery high", "PC connected", and "Phone 1 connected".
The dongle LED does not illuminate or flash at any time.

Based on the above, the headset itself appears to be working, but the USB dongle is either not being detected by Windows or may have failed.

Could you please investigate and advise on the next steps, including whether the dongle may require replacement?

Unfortunately, I am unable to call the Service Desk using the headset because it is not available as an audio device when connected via the dongle.

Good afternoon,

I hope this email finds you well.

Thank you for all your assistance in setting up the initial secure SharePoint for the Commonwealth Teaching Scholarships (CTS) Program last year. The site has been extremely helpful and has functioned according to the program’s requirements.

As the CTS Program moves into Round 2, we have been discussing the logistic of record management. We have received an increased level of interest in Round 2 and expect to receive a significantly larger volume of applications and personal files (possibly upwards of 5000 applications).

The CTS team were wondering if it would be possible to set up a second secure SharePoint for the management and storage of Round 2 applicant information please? This will help minimise potential mishandling of Round 1 documents and make ongoing management of Round 1 and 2 applications easier. If possible, I have detailed our specifications below:

Upcoming program: Commonwealth Teaching Scholarships
Round Two is scheduled to open at the end of Nov 2024 and run until 2028.

Asking for:

description:
Hi Team

Our branch will shortly be transitioning to a new organisational structure. While there are no new staff joining the branch, existing staff will be moving into newly established teams with new team names.

We are seeking advice on the best approach to updating our SharePoint Branch Home Page, team pages, document libraries, folders and permissions to align with the new structure.

Some staff have expressed concerns that moving folders or reorganising content may result in files being lost or become difficult to locate. We would appreciate your guidance on:


  *   Recommended approaches for updating SharePoint following a restructure.
  *   Whether existing folders and document libraries can remain in place with updated navigation and team names.
  *   Potential risks associated with moving folders or content.
  *   Any impacts on file access, permissions, links and version history.
  *   Suggested practices for transitioning to the new structure while minimising disruption to staff.

If there are any tools, templates or support services available to assist with this transition, we would be grateful for your advice.

Thank you for your assistance.

Emma Campbell

short_description: Secure deletion of identifiable data - JSA interviews
description:
Hi Team,

Without a JSA specific policy that relates to retention and destruction of data, I am seeking your advice with the destruction of interview data please.

The project involves a qualitative research component that will involve phone interviewing and recording survey respondents that agree to be recontacted.

As JSA staff will be conducting the interviews and no external data sharing is required. The team will use a limited user access library within SharePoint to store these identifiable interviews instead.

My question to you is firstly, what is the policy around secure deletion of data and retention periods and secondly, when it comes to performing secure deletion on SharePoint (emptying first and second stage recycle bins), are we able to do both and confirm absolute deletion has occurred, or do we need to specify the retention period eg. 5 years for the second stage recycle bin, in our privacy and ethics documents because we cannot delete second-stage due to policy?

I have read the Data and Information Retention and Disposal Policy and DEWR's Information Security Policy and couldn't find the answer I'm after.

description:
Hi Cyber Security,

I would like to report a recurring issue with CyberArk RDP session window management that occurs intermittently but frequently enough to be repeatable.

Occasionally, after resizing or changing the display state of a CyberArk-launched RDP session, the window can no longer be maximised correctly. Subject: RE: National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) Data Retention query [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Julie,

In response to Frankie's questions, we have outlined some general considerations relating to data ownership, storage, and retention/disposal. These are general answers, to give a more accurate answer would require understanding the application of Commonwealth and State / Territory laws onto an example.

One consideration is the potential complexity when involving State and Territory data held by the Commonwealth. The arrangement between Cth and State / Territory for NCVER would require involvement from legal areas.

In any event, here are the general principles:

Data Ownership
The primary consideration is to identify the appropriate custodian of the dataset. Within DEWR, data ownership in the Data Asset Register lists the custodian of known assets within the department. A custodian is responsible for the accountability and management of the dataset. It is possible for an organisation to hold or use data without being the owner or custodian of that data. We have examples of data / datasets hosted internally that DEWR is not the custodian of, eg. CRN is a piece of data we utilise but don't have custodianship of.

In the case of the national VET dataset, clarification would be required regarding whether custodianship remains with contributing jurisdictions or sits with NCVER as the national VET data custodian. There are two NCVER datasets in our Data Asset Register currently, which can be found by filtering on "Data Custodian" (Column G).

Data Assets, Aristotle & Microsoft Purview<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/dewr-rad/SitePages/Data-Assets.aspx>

Storage
Storage solutions and system-specific capabilities sit outside the Data Governance function. DEWR policy requires information assets to be stored in approved systems that support recordkeeping, accessibility, and compliance obligations under the Archives Act 1983 (Cth). We would likely defer to you in Information Management or a technology division for this aspect [Store | SharePoint]<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/SitePages/Store.aspx?isSPOFile=1>

Retention and Disposal
For retention and disposal, we principally take direction from the Archives Act 1983 but there will be specific obligations in other sources, which are a case by case question. Long term preservation, archiving, or disposal will need considerations of legislation, business value, research value, and agreements covering the data. National Archives of Australia guidance on retention and disposal of data and datasets is the best starting point. Whether NCVER assumes responsibility for retention and disposal of the national dataset, the applicability of Commonwealth archival arrangements, and any ongoing state and territory obligations are likely to require records management and legal advice.

Subject: National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) Data Retention query [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Information Management,
National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) has recently raised a question regarding the long-term retention of historical VET datasets and how information of this nature should be managed into the future.
NCVER is the national custodian of Vocational Education and Training (VET) data, collecting and maintaining data submitted by States and Territories across Australia. NCVER also produces a range of statistical publications, research outputs and reporting that support governments, policymakers and the VET sector.
I have spoken with Richard about the possibility of bringing the NCVER data into the DEWR Content Manager environment as a potential long-term retention solution. However, it is unclear whether this would be appropriate given NCVER's status as an independent organisation and its role as the national VET data custodian.
From both a records management and policy perspective, we would appreciate advice on the following:

  *   What retention, archival or preservation considerations should be taken into account for long-term historical datasets?
  *   Are there archival, read-only or cold-storage options that could be considered where the data is no longer required within operational systems but may continue to have historical, research, reporting or evidentiary value?
  *   Once data has been submitted to NCVER and incorporated into a national dataset, does the ongoing management of that data remain subject to individual State and Territory recordkeeping requirements, or does NCVER assume responsibility for its retention, archival management and disposal?
  *   If responsibility sits with NCVER, could the management of the national dataset be aligned with the Commonwealth Archives Act framework, rather than requiring ongoing consideration of individual State and Territory retention and disposal requirements?
  *   Could NCVER potentially retain and archive these datasets in its capacity as the national VET data custodian?
  *   From an information management perspective, is there merit in a national custodianship model whereby NCVER retains and manages historical VET datasets on behalf of the sector?
  *   If such an approach were considered appropriate, what governance, retention, archival, ownership and access arrangements would be required to support it?
  *   What cost, compliance and risk considerations should be taken into account when assessing the available options?
We acknowledge that some of these questions may extend beyond records management and into matters of ownership, custodianship and legislative responsibility. As such, NCVER may wish to seek its own legal advice regarding any obligations or opportunities associated with the long-term retention and management of nationally significant VET datasets.
Our intent is not to determine a preferred outcome at this stage, but rather to ensure that all relevant considerations have been explored before any decisions are made regarding the future management, preservation or disposal of these datasets.
We are particularly interested in understanding whether there is a more consistent national approach that supports the long-term preservation of historically significant VET information while balancing governance, accessibility and cost.
Thank you for your assistance and guidance.
Kind regards,

Frankie Kenny

short_description: Assistance Required – Remediation of new Spring Framework Vulnerability in Commvault ContentStore
description:
Dear Team,

I would like to share the vulnerability details identified in Commvault ContentStore and request further investigation and remediation.

Spring Framework 5.3.x < 5.3.49 / 6.1.x < 6.1.28 / 6.2.x < 6.2.18.1 / 7.0.x < 7.0.7.1 Multiple Vulnerabilities (320777):

Synopsis
The Spring Framework install on the remote host is affected by multiple vulnerabilities.

Description
The version of Spring Framework installed on the remote host is 5.3.x prior to 5.3.49, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.28, 6.2.x prior to 6.2.18.1, or 7.0.x prior to 7.0.7.1. It is, therefore, affected by multiple vulnerabilities:

- IDs for WebSocket sessions in the spring-websocket module are not cryptographically unpredictable, which may be possible to exploit in combination with inadequate authorization rules. (CVE-2026-41838)

- Applications may be vulnerable to a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attack if an attacker is able to provide a pattern which is then directly or indirectly supplied to one of the following methods in AntPathMatcher:
match, matchStart, extractUriTemplateVariables. (CVE-2026-41848)

- In an untrusted JMS environment, org.springframework.jms.support.converter.MappingJackson2MessageConverter and org.springframework.jms.support.converter.JacksonJsonMessageConverter allow arbitrary class instantiation, which can lead to unauthorized actions via gadget class deserialization. (CVE-2026-41855)

Note that Nessus has not tested for these issues but has instead relied only on the application's self-reported version number.

Steps to Remediate
Upgrade to Spring Framework version 5.3.49, 6.1.28, 6.2.18.1, or 7.0.7.1 or later.

Please see completed form for New Starter Narelle Johnson.

The version of Spring Framework installed on the remote host is 5.3.x prior to 5.3.49, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.28, 6.2.x prior to 6.2.18.1, or 7.0.x prior to 7.0.7.1. It is, therefore, affected by multiple vulnerabilities:

- IDs for WebSocket sessions in the spring-websocket module are not cryptographically unpredictable, which may be possible to exploit in combination with inadequate authorization rules. (CVE-2026-41838)

- Applications may be vulnerable to a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attack if an attacker is able to provide a pattern which is then directly or indirectly supplied to one of the following methods in AntPathMatcher:
match, matchStart, extractUriTemplateVariables. (CVE-2026-41848)

- In an untrusted JMS environment, org.springframework.jms.support.converter.MappingJackson2MessageConverter and org.springframework.jms.support.converter.JacksonJsonMessageConverter allow arbitrary class instantiation, which can lead to unauthorized actions via gadget class deserialization. (CVE-2026-41855)

Note that Nessus has not tested for these issues but has instead relied only on the application's self-reported version number.

Steps to Remediate
Upgrade to Spring Framework version 5.3.49, 6.1.28, 6.2.18.1, or 7.0.7.1 or later.

Hi IT Team,
The Integrity and Fraud Team is drafting a proposal to our AS for a dedicated workstation which will seek to support authorised open-source intelligence (OSINT), integrity, fraud, misconduct, insider threat and security-related activities. The workstation is to be shared between our team and 1 or 2 other teams in the branch/division.
Please note that we only need one.
The proposed capability would support a range of activities, including:

  *   Conducting OSINT research using publicly available information sources.
  *   Reviewing information available through social media platforms, professional networking sites, company websites, public registers and media reporting.
  *   Identifying associations and relationships between individuals, entities and organisations.
  *   Supporting fraud, corruption, misconduct, conflict of interest and security-related investigations.
  *   Undertaking insider threat and personnel security assessments.
  *   Verifying information provided through complaints, tip-offs and intelligence reporting.
  *   Supporting intelligence development, environmental scanning and risk assessments.
  *   Conducting basic link analysis and developing intelligence products.
Before proceeding with the proposal, we would appreciate your advice on the technical feasibility and practical setup requirements. At this stage, we're not seeking a detailed assessment of the business benefits, but rather guidance to help inform the proposal and ensure any suggested solution aligns with departmental ICT requirements. Specifically, we would appreciate advice on:

  *   What a suitable workstation setup would look like (hardware, network access, security controls, user access arrangements, etc.).
  *   Whether a standalone device would be required, or if there are alternative ICT-supported options available.
  *   Any ICT security, governance, audit logging or compliance considerations that should be factored into the proposal.

Hi Records Management Team,

The Department currently receives Single Touch Payroll (STP) data from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) under a data-sharing arrangement to support administration of the Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System. The data is used to assist with claim assessment and payment verification, targeted compliance activities, and verification of apprenticeship cessation/end dates.

As part of ongoing governance work on the joint data share arrangement with the ATO, I have been looking into developing a proposed STP data destruction approach that would:

  *   Retain evidentiary snapshots of STP information used to support business decisions and audit requirements;
  *   Destroy raw STP data once it is no longer required for operational purposes and any applicable retention requirements have been met; and
  *   Remove replicated copies of raw STP data from downstream systems, including reporting and data warehouse environments.

To ensure the proposed approach complies with the Archives Act 1983 and applicable records management requirements, I would appreciate your advice on the questions below, or guidance on the appropriate area or contact who can assist with this advice.


  1.  Is STP data received from the ATO and used to support:

     *   Apprenticeship incentive claim assessment and payment decisions;
     *   compliance activities; and
     *   apprenticeship cessation/end date verification

considered a Commonwealth record for the purposes of the Archives Act 1983?


  1.  Is this information covered by an existing DEWR Records Authority, General Records Authority, or other approved disposal authority?


  1.  If so, could you please advise:

     *   the applicable disposal class(es);
     *   if there is a minimum retention period(s);
     *   any requirements or conditions relating to the destruction of the data; and
     *   whether destruction of the source/raw STP data is authorised once retention requirements have been met.


  1.  We are proposing to retain evidentiary "snapshots" of STP information used in decision-making (for example, claim assessment snapshots and apprenticeship cessation snapshots) while destroying the underlying raw STP dataset after the authorised retention period expires. Would retention of these snapshots satisfy recordkeeping and audit requirements, or would additional information need to be retained?


  1.  The proposed solution would also remove any replicated copies of the raw STP data held in downstream systems, including reporting and data warehouse environments. Are there any records management considerations or approvals required for destruction of these copies?


  1.  Are there any other legislative, audit, or information management requirements that should be considered when defining the retention and destruction approach for Departmental data (STP data)?

I'm seeking this advice to inform how we undertake data destruction on STP data that has been shared with us from the ATO and ensure it aligns with the Department requirements and Archives Act 1983.

As mentioned if this is not the right team please let me know who might be best to discuss this with.

Thanks
Linda

short_description: FW: Approaching SharePoint Site Storage Limit
description:
HI team

We have received notifications that the DEWR-TargetedComplianceFrameworkTCFAssurance-TEAM SharePoint site is approaching its storage limit.

We have already undertaken some housekeeping activities, including removing unnecessary documents and emptying the recycle bin. While this has provided some temporary relief, we expect the issue to continue due to the nature of our assurance work.

The TCF Assurance team undertakes second line assurance activities and is required to capture and retain evidence for analysis. In many cases, relying on links to documents stored in other SharePoint locations is not suitable, as those source documents remain open to amendment. To maintain an accurate record of the evidence assessed at a specific point in time, we need to retain copies of the documents that formed the basis of our assurance activities.

In addition, we are required to retain the evidence we have collected and analysed to support potential future reviews, including Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) audits and internal audit activities. This means that our storage requirements will continue to grow over time as assurance activities are completed.

Given these requirements, could you please advise on the most appropriate long-term solution? Specifically:

  *   Is it possible to increase the storage allocation for the existing SharePoint site?
  *   Alternatively, is there an approved archive solution that would allow us to retain historical assurance evidence while maintaining accessibility for future audit or review purposes?
  *   Are there any records management or SharePoint best-practice approaches that would better support this type of evidentiary storage requirement?

We would appreciate your advice on the most suitable option to ensure we can continue to meet our assurance and audit obligations while managing storage constraints.

Thanks

short_description: New CyberArk Safe and Movement of existing account to new Safe
description:
Hi team,

Could this request please be forwarded to IT Security, specifically Karen Sibraa (cc'ed).

We'd like to create a new safe called SE-DSD-ECPS-D under "DEWR - Digital Service Contact Centre (DSCC) - DEV" and move existing account Service_SLnk_NP from current safe SE-DSD-ECP-D to new safe SE-DSD-ECPS-D

Business case:
A new CyberArk safe is required to store and manage service accounts associated with the Synapse platform in non-production environments. Currently, Synapse-related accounts are stored alongside other non-production service accounts within the generic Dev safe. As the non-production landscape continues to mature and additional platform-specific service accounts are introduced, maintaining all accounts within a single safe increases administrative overhead and reduces clarity around ownership, access management, and account lifecycle management.
Creating a dedicated non production synapse safe will:

  *   Improve segregation of privileged accounts by platform and purpose.
  *   Simplify access management by granting Synapse administrators access only to accounts relevant to their responsibilities.
  *   Reduce the risk of unnecessary access to unrelated service accounts.
  *   Improve auditability and reporting by clearly identifying Synapse-related privileged accounts.
  *   Provide a scalable structure for future growth as additional platform-specific safes are introduced.

This request aligns with the principle of least privilege and supports ongoing improvements in privileged account governance, security, and operational management within the non-production environment.

Regards
Demerson

We'd appreciate any advice on the availability, suitability and supportability of these approaches, as well as any lessons learnt from DEWR's experience.
For example, could you help us understand the following:
